title: ARIA Roles on Native Elements
code: <button role="button">Click</button>

bugs.explanation: Adding `role="button"` to a `<button>` element is redundant — the native element already has the implicit ARIA role of `button`. Redundant roles add verbosity without benefit. Use native HTML semantics and only add ARIA roles when no native equivalent exists.

title: aria-hidden on Focusable Element
code: Profile

bugs.fix: Profile Profile
bugs.explanation: `aria-hidden="true"` hides an element from the accessibility tree but keeps it in the DOM. If the element is focusable (an `<a>` with `href`), keyboard users can still tab to it — an invisible, non-accessible focusable trap. Add `tabindex="-1"` to remove it from tab order if using `aria-hidden`.

title: aria-required vs required
code:
<form>
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input type="email" id="email" aria-required="true">
</form>

bugs.explanation: Both `aria-required` and `required` communicate that a field is mandatory, but `required` also enables native browser validation. Use the native `required` attribute; the browser will also map it to `aria-required` implicitly. Only use `aria-required` if native validation is disabled (`novalidate`) or unavailable.

bugs.explanation: The `listbox` role requires child `option` elements. Adding `role="listbox"` to a `<ul>` without also adding `role="option"` to `<li>` children creates an invalid ARIA tree. Each list item needs `role="option"`.

bugs.explanation: Focus order must follow a logical reading order (WCAG 2.4.3). Placing the skip link after the modal in DOM order means keyboard users encounter modal buttons before the skip link, which is wrong. DOM order determines focus order for `tabindex="0"` elements.
